findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave: displaced stone drainage components and uncertain hydraulic function
findings.assertion: Sload reports that stone drains and covers were found on the cave surface near blockages when the cave was documented in the 1970s, with reused pieces embedded in later consolidation. Figure 8.14 captions a 120-cm-long rhyolite drain in front of Blockage 8 and two drain covers at Blockage 9. Their original configuration and the way water entered or circulated in the cave are not archaeologically established. Sload reports that the proposed natural spring was challenged by TE28 excavations and later palaeohydrological studies.
findings.geography: Artificial cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, State of Mexico, Mexico
findings.source_title: Rebecca Sload (2020), The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan
findings.exact_locator: Printed pp.138–141, 'Drains and Drain Covers', Figure 8.14 caption (120 cm rhyolite drain at Blockage 8; two covers at Blockage 9); original Baker et al. 1974:10–11 and Manzanilla hydrology publications not examined
findings.examined_material: Published text and photographic caption; figure itself NOT visually examined because screenshot retrieval timed out
findings.limitations: Location of displaced stones does not establish an assembled functioning water system; statement about absent spring is a published synthesis, not independently checked against palaeohydrological source; ritual water use remains a hypothesis.
findings.educational_use: Site dossier: distinguish excavated stone components from conjectured ritual water system.

findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave: missing TE28 artifact specimens in 2006 laboratory review
findings.assertion: During her initial laboratory review in 2006, Sload could not locate four shell small finds (worked and unworked), one mica specimen and three worked-obsidian specimens from the Area B/B:NE terminus collection. She separately reports that all twelve obsidian artifacts catalogued from TE28 were missing at that review, whereas obsidian from the 1977 surface collection was present. The three terminus obsidian objects are part of the twelve, not twelve additional losses.
findings.geography: Area B and B:NE terminus of artificial cave under Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, State of Mexico, Mexico
findings.source_title: Rebecca Sload (2020), The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan
findings.exact_locator: Printed pp.119–120, Chapter 8, 'What Happened During Initial Use?' introductory artifact inventory and its Spanish translation
findings.examined_material: Published English and Spanish paragraphs checked; underlying 1978 collections inventory and 2006 laboratory records not independently accessed
findings.evidence_type: Museum/archaeological collection provenance audit reported by study author
findings.limitations: Unavailable at the 2006 review is not proof of permanent loss; present-day storage and catalog accession numbers are unverified. Do not claim that the artifacts' ancient function is established.
findings.educational_use: Evidence-quality sidebar: limits of interpretations when an excavated collection cannot be reexamined.
